did_you_know.text: Did you know? The outer gate of the sanctuary facing east was commanded to remain closed because the LORD, the God of Israel, had entered through it.
Did you know? The prince is the only one mentioned as sitting at the gate and eating bread before the LORD; he enters through the gate’s portico and leaves the same way.
Did you know? Ezekiel is instructed to pay special attention to the laws of the temple, its regulations, and the ways of entering and leaving the sanctuary.
Did you know? The Levites who turned away from the LORD when Israel worshiped idols bear the consequences of their sin, so their duties in the sanctuary are limited.

Did you know? The Levites whose duties were restricted serve as gatekeepers and ministers of the temple, and they slaughter the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people; however, they are not described as offering sacrifices before the LORD like the priests.
Did you know? The descendants of Zadok are given the central responsibility for the holy service because they faithfully guarded the sanctuary when the Israelites went astray.
Did you know? When serving at the gates of the inner court and inside the temple, the priests are commanded to wear linen garments, not wool.
Did you know? One of the priests’ duties is to teach the people to distinguish between what is holy and what is common, and between what is unclean and what is clean.
Did you know? The priests are required to preside over the people’s disputes, judge according to the LORD’s laws, observe His regulations and statutes, and keep His Sabbaths holy.
Did you know? The priests do not receive a regular inheritance in Israel because the LORD Himself is their inheritance and possession.
